title: Pulse Day integration plan & team commitment letters v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working runbook for the upcoming ‘Pulse Day’ (company-wide alignment day) — it bundles the all-hands flow, a short exec update script, a set of draft OKRs to test during the event, and a lightweight template for 'team commitment letters' each functional lead will publish after the session. Aim: create a fast feedback loop so we finish Pulse Day with concrete, timeboxed commitments and a short risk / rollback plan for the top 3 cross-company experiments.

Context and constraints:
- Timing: 1/2 day sync + 90m all-hands + 60m small-team breakouts.
- Audience: ~150 employees across Engineering, Product, Research, GTM, Ops.
- Decision hygiene: no new long-lived OKRs introduced during Pulse Day; we will prioritize and propose addenda to the quarter slate.
- What we want from teams: a single page "commitment letter" (see template below) that includes concrete deliverables, owner, confidence score, and rollback criteria.

High-level agenda (working):
1) 09:00 - Kickoff (Founders) — 10m: brief tone-setting + one-sentence restatement of the company thesis
2) 09:10 - Exec update (Product + Infra leads) — 20m: two slides each: 1 metric that matters, 1 risk we are watching, 1 ask of other teams
3) 09:35 - Focus slate (company-ops) — 15m: top 6 cross-company bets for next 6 weeks
4) 09:50 - Breakout instructions — 5m: pre-assigned rooms (GTM/product/infra), deliver a commitment letter
5) 10:00 - Breakouts — 60m: teams complete letters + signal blockers in tracker
6) 11:05 - Rapid report-outs — 45m: 2m per breakouts + red/amber/green flags
7) 11:50 - Closing + next steps (CEO) — 10m: who signs, where artifacts live

Draft exec update script (bullet-style for rehearsals):
- CEO: 90s — market snapshot, where we are winning, 1 ask to the company
- CTO: 4m — serving runtime health, latency/cost trend, top mitigation (eg, burst capacity policy rollout)
- VP Product: 4m — product adoption signals, one experiment we will accelerate, one customer ask we must address
- Head of Sales: 2m — pipeline heatmap and one operational ask from product/infra

OKR draft slate to test (short, drafty):
- Objective A: Make Redwood the predictable inference platform for small-to-mid product teams.
  - KR A1: Reduce median single-request p95 latency for hosted-API by 25% on text-gen workloads in core regions.
  - KR A2: Achieve <$0.0008 per embedding unit on classic embedding workload via batching + cache improvements.
- Objective B: Enterprise-ready Private deployments with audit-first launch path.
  - KR B1: Complete KMS integration + E2E test suite for private package (3 regions).
  - KR B2: Validate 2 pilot customers on air-gapped package with SLAs.
- Objective C: Cost/perf toolkit adoption
  - KR C1: 10 internal product routes using Redwood Optimize suggestions; measure token-cost delta.

Team commitment letter template (deliverable each breakout must produce; 1 page max):
- Team: <team name>
- Owners: <primary, backup>
- Commitment (1 sentence): <what we deliver in 6 weeks>
- Success metrics (2): <metric + target>
- Confidence (1-5): <number>
- Blockers/Dependencies: <explicit teams or infra needs>
- Rollback / fallback criteria: <when to abort and who to notify>
- Sign-off: <lead + date>

Cross-company risk heatmap (top 3 experiments):
1) Model-variant fallback policy (risk: regression in quality when falling back)
   - Mitigation: add canary prompts, automated eval threshold; rollback: pin to previous variant and enable routing to dedicated capacity.
2) Aggressive batching/caching changes (risk: tail latency spikes)
   - Mitigation: phased rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) + synthetic spike test; rollback: revert batching config and enable temporary autoscale.
3) Private deploy package ramp (risk: long lead time for customer onboarding)
   - Mitigation: pre-built onboarding checklist + customer engineering slot reserve; rollback: offer hosted/dedicated bridge for pilots.

Communications and artifacts after Pulse Day:
- Each team's commitment letter lives in a single folder: /shared_drives/company/misc/pulse-day-commitments/ (create + link)
- Exec update (slides & script) uploaded to Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-PLANS-4821
- Action tracker: JIRA-PULSE-110 (sprint with tickets created automatically)
- Short post-event survey (1 slide): gather confidence and additional blockers

Immediate action items (before Pulse Day):
- @Marco: finalize breakout assignments + create meeting rooms (due 2026-02-18)
- @Jinsoo: prepare infra canary prompts + synthetic tests (due 2026-02-18)
- @Lauren: build the Confluence page & template for commitment letters (due 2026-02-17)
- @Omar: draft the all-hands Slack thread + FAQ stub (due 2026-02-19)

Open questions / trade-offs (notes to self):
- Do we allow teams to add a new OKR if it is mission-critical? (hold: add via opt-in gating)
- How strict should rollback windows be for infra changes tied to the all-hands slate? (propose 48h autorevert if anomaly)

Appendix (quick skeleton for a team letter example):
- Team: Serving Runtime
- Owners: Jinsoo Park (primary), Mei Nguyen (backup)
- Commitment: Rollout KV prefix caching for the top 3 model routes to drop token cost by 12% in 6 wks.
- Success metrics: p95 latency delta < +10ms; token-cost delta -12%
- Confidence: 3/5
- Blockers: kernel tuning slot + QA cluster access (Infra)
- Rollback: disable cache and revert to current threshold if p95 latency > baseline + 15ms for 30m
- Sign-off: Jinsoo Park, 2026-02-20

Notes (informal):
- Keep this doc minimal; the goal of Pulse Day is commitments not perfect plans.
- During breakouts, encourage teams to call out "quick wins" vs "platform bets" — we want both but different review cadence.
- We should include an explicit note about customer payrolls/enterprise audits if any team’s commit touches private deployments.

If you are editing: leave comments inline with your name and keep the call-to-action bullets at the top updated.
